purpose: ORT Web WASM rung for INT4 Nemotron 3.5 — final status

result.wasmText: And so my fellow Americans ask not what your country can do for you at what you can do for your country. <en-US>
result.nativeText: And so my fellow Americans ask not what your country can do for you at what you can do for your country
result.note: WASM == native for the full 41-token native sequence; WASM emits 3 extra trailing tokens ('.', '<en-US>') at the exhausted-frames boundary. NeMo oracle text has the same '. <en-US>' segment structure.

history.blocker: Original blocker: ORT Web WASM in Node cannot load external ONNX data files ('Module.MountedFiles is not available').
history.resolution: Repacked INT4 models to single-file ONNX (onnx.load(load_external_data=True) + onnx.save(save_as_external_data=False)) into N:/models/onnx/nemo/nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-int4-singles/ (encoder 660 MB, decoder 57 MB, joint 36 MB).

history.blocker: Second blocker (false alarm): WASM/node pipeline appeared to diverge from Python ORT (encoder cos 0.07, all-blank step 0). Investigated as suspected ORT 1.23.2 vs 1.25+/1.29 numerical regression across MatMulNBits, Conv, graph optimization levels, and graph-prefix bisects.
history.resolution: Root cause was a harness bug, NOT a runtime difference: dump_nemo_mel.py saves _tmp_mel.npy with fortran_order=True; the JS parseNpy ignored the flag and read column-major data as row-major, feeding scrambled mel to WASM/node. Python probes used np.load (honors fortran_order) and were correct. After fixing parseNpy to transpose fortran-order data, WASM produced token-identical output to native ORT.

lessons: ORT Web WASM in Node requires single-file ONNX models (no external data) — or a browser harness where Emscripten's mounted files work.
When native and JS harnesses share .npy fixtures, JS parsers MUST honor fortran_order; a C-order misread silently scrambles 2-D arrays and mimics numerical-parity failures.
Single-op A/B models (MatMulNBits, Conv) and graph-prefix truncations confirmed ORT 1.23.2 / 1.25-dev / 1.29.0 compute this model identically when inputs match.
